Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

lose verb

a thing: no longer have it

also lose something, I’ve lost it, be lost, it’s lost, go missing, lost (a lost thing), forget (a name)

classical

Cic. Sen. 11: nisi tū āmīsissēs

āmittō, āmittere, āmīsī, āmissum

verb, third conjugation

lose, let slip

First “let go”, and so to lose what one had, by mischance as much as by fault.

Other words

  • perdō, perdere, perdidī, perditum — lose for good; waste

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Ter. Ph. 386: nōmen perdidī; Vulg. Lc. 15.4: sī perdiderit ūnam ex illīs; Traupman 342

    To lose utterly, or throw away (operam perdere, to waste one’s effort); nōmen perdidī, I’ve forgotten the name. Its passive is pereō.

  • pereō, perīre, periī, peritum — be lost, go missing

    verb, irregular, conjugated like eō: the passive of perdō · also used · classical · Vulg. Lc. 15.6: ovem meam, quae perierat

    Lewis & Short: as the passive of perdō only pereō, perditus, perīre are in good use. So “it was lost” is perierat; in comedy Periī! is “I’m done for”.

Examples

  • Ubi pilam āmīsistī?

    Where did you lose the ball?composed

  • ‘certē,’ inquit rīdēns, ‘nam nisi tū āmīsissēs, numquam recēpissem’

    “Certainly,” he said with a smile, “for if you hadn’t lost it, I should never have taken it back.”Cic. Sen. 11

  • Periī hercle: nōmen perdidī.

    Oh no: I’ve forgotten the name.Ter. Ph. 386

  • sī perdiderit ūnam ex illīs … Congrātulāminī mihi, quia invēnī ovem meam, quae perierat.

    if he loses one of them … “Rejoice with me, for I have found my sheep that was lost.”Vulg. Lc. 15.4–6

See also lose, get lost, I’m done for!, find.
